stages.request:
Item costs are written to the data file as decimal strings like "2.50", and our finance import can't read them. Please store each item's cost as a whole number of cents in a `cost_cents` field instead of `unit_cost`, and raise the data file's `version` to 2. Files written at version 1 must keep working: they should open as before and come out in the new form the next time they are saved.

People still enter and see costs in dollars and cents.

I mistyped a transfer as `stockroom transfer BOLT-M6 5 A1 A1`, and afterwards A1 showed 5 more bolts than it had before; `stockroom check` then reported a mismatch for BOLT-M6 at A1.

A transfer whose source and destination are the same location should be refused with `cannot transfer within one location: A1` (with that location's code) and should change nothing.

When scripting against the library, `Inventory.on_hand(sku)` only gives me a grand total. Please make it return a dict mapping each location code to the quantity held there, leaving out locations that hold none of the item, and add `Inventory.total(sku)` returning the grand total (0 when nothing is held). Both should refuse an unknown SKU with the usual `unknown item: <sku>` error.

Our scanner app logs which movement each library call produced. Please make `Inventory.receive`, `issue`, `transfer` and `adjust` return the `seq` of the movement they record instead of a quantity. Nothing else about how stockroom behaves should change.

Our warehouse system imports the movement log from the data file and needs every line to touch exactly one location. Record each movement as lines carrying a `location` and a signed `delta` (positive for goods coming in, negative for goods going out) in place of `qty`, `from` and `to`. A transfer becomes two lines, out of the source and into the destination, sharing the transfer's `seq`.

Raise the file `version` to 3; version 1 and 2 files must still open and be rewritten in the new form when saved. Nothing else about how stockroom behaves should change.

Some of our bins are small. Let locations have an optional capacity: `stockroom add-location C3 --capacity 50` on the command line and a `capacity` argument to `Inventory.add_location`. Without one, a location has no limit.

A receive or transfer that would leave a location holding more units than its capacity, counting every item stored there, must be refused with `location C3 is full: capacity 50, would hold 60` and change nothing. Keep the capacity on the location in the data file as `capacity`, null when there is no limit.
